<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
The code cells run real commands against this repo, so the key claims are
shown, not just stated.</cell id="cell-0">
<cell id="cell-1"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already

<cell id="cell-3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, five CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, and (since L20, 2026-06-12) `fcsr` - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie` - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`.</cell id="cell-3">

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported since L6 was resolved 2026-06-13; the engine's RTL must
  implement it, or the resume aborts loudly. No privilege CHANGE inside
  the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET, both outside the envelope)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie` (L2). PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege
  handoffs (L6, 2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret,
fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified after write) and
the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore, and the plugin's drain-at-exit record became
  context-free so the SimPoint profile pass works with the SimControl exit
  path (`tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_at_exit.sh`). The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run
still produces a clean `window_cycles` figure:</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8">!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
    --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf</cell id="cell-8">

<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory
  regions (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries, but an M-mode resume writes none of them back. vsim runs the
  ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1 silently disappears.
- Partial since L6 (2026-06-13): an S/U-privilege resume DOES mirror the
  producer's PMP block (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`;
  tolerant writes, entries beyond what the hart implements no-op),
  because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access
  faults - an S/U ROI could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - the mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode handoffs; locked-entry semantics
  untested).

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bit: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary was silently measured in M-mode (both sides
  hardcoded `priv = 3`; DCSR.prv was never written, so `dret` always
  resumed in M-mode).
- Status: RESOLVED 2026-06-13. The privilege now round-trips:
  - QEMU plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` virtual register
    (`hybrid_handoff.c`).
  - `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` and reads
    it back: an RTL without S/U (the default `ax45mpv_premium` has
    `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) WARL-pins the field and the resume
    aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error instead of measuring
    the wrong privilege. Reserved `priv=2` is rejected up front.
  - For S/U states the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + 8 even
    `pmpcfg`, addr before cfg) is mirrored into the hart first: with PMP

    the L2 slice S/U execution cannot run without).
  - `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` at the exit halt, so the drained file
    records the privilege the ROI actually ran in, and `--verify`
    compares it against the QEMU oracle.

  paging stays off (L3), and S-mode CSRs are still not transported -- an

  S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`.

<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L7. No check that the workload fits guest RAM; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

  `--mem-size` sizes every leg up to 2G (driver mmap = QEMU memory backend
  = vsim RAM window), so the old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap"
  was misleading. The real limitation is the missing fit check plus the
  2 GiB ceiling.

  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption or a confusing crash; nothing tells the user `--mem-size` was
  the cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the
  driver pre-caps at the same value -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Also unchecked: the V scratch region (4 KiB at GPA `0x00FF0000`) sits
  inside RAM and nothing verifies the ELF avoids it; a segment overlapping
  it is clobbered by the V sweep on hybrid V runs.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:175` (128 MB default) and `:183` (2G pre-cap);

  check); `verilator/src/main.cpp:414` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`). The driver already parses ELF headers for PC
  resolution (`driver/elf_syms.hpp`), so a PT_LOAD-vs-mem-size startup
  check would be cheap to add.
- Status: OPEN (the fit check). Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough
  by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5); > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart

  timer / software / external interrupt (anything NOT caused by the current
  instruction). Synchronous exceptions (`ecall`, illegal, `mret`) ARE
  supported - this is only about async interrupts.

  (QEMU is functional with no real cycles, the RTL is cycle-accurate), so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.

  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.

- Status: OPEN. Designed fix is the opt-in `--cosim-async` mode (the RTL

| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding (rt_c_fcsr) and S/U-privilege (rt_priv_*) covered now; still no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** ~~`fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip
   (L20)~~ - resolved 2026-06-12; `fcsr` now transports and `--verify`
   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** ~~M-mode only~~ (S/U privilege
   transports since L6, 2026-06-13, on an S/U-capable engine), but "no
   traps, no paging, no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L5) still
   rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any
   driver code, anything with page faults. The vplat runtime covers
   bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 5 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle,
   minstret, fcsr), plus `dcsr.prv` and - for S/U handoffs - the PMP
   block (L6, 2026-06-13). `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`, `mscratch`,
   `mip/mie` (and PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never written
   back into vsim (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata ate 16 bytes, fcsr another
   8; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.</cell id="cell-17">

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
The code cells run real commands against this repo, so the key claims are
shown, not just stated.

## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andes-sim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the
QEMU plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing, run
`source ./setup.sh` from the repo root.

import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, five CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, and (since L20, 2026-06-12) `fcsr` - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie` - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported since L6 was resolved 2026-06-13; the engine's RTL must
  implement it, or the resume aborts loudly. No privilege CHANGE inside
  the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET, both outside the envelope)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie` (L2). PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege
  handoffs (L6, 2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret,
fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified after write) and
the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore, and the plugin's drain-at-exit record became
  context-free so the SimPoint profile pass works with the SimControl exit
  path (`tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_at_exit.sh`). The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run
still produces a clean `window_cycles` figure:

!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
    --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory
  regions (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries, but an M-mode resume writes none of them back. vsim runs the
  ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1 silently disappears.
- Partial since L6 (2026-06-13): an S/U-privilege resume DOES mirror the
  producer's PMP block (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`;
  tolerant writes, entries beyond what the hart implements no-op),
  because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access
  faults - an S/U ROI could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - the mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode handoffs; locked-entry semantics
  untested).

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).
  Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX set before
  the enter marker, in-ROI self-check, distinct sentinel captured at the
  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`).

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bit: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary was silently measured in M-mode (both sides
  hardcoded `priv = 3`; DCSR.prv was never written, so `dret` always
  resumed in M-mode).
- Status: RESOLVED 2026-06-13. The privilege now round-trips:
  - QEMU plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` virtual register
    (`hybrid_handoff.c`).
  - `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` and reads
    it back: an RTL without S/U (the default `ax45mpv_premium` has
    `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) WARL-pins the field and the resume
    aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error instead of measuring
    the wrong privilege. Reserved `priv=2` is rejected up front.
  - For S/U states the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + 8 even
    `pmpcfg`, addr before cfg) is mirrored into the hart first: with PMP
    implemented and no matching entry, every S/U access faults (this is
    the L2 slice S/U execution cannot run without).
  - `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` at the exit halt, so the drained file
    records the privilege the ROI actually ran in, and `--verify`
    compares it against the QEMU oracle.
- Residual envelope: the ROI must stay in ONE privilege (no traps/xRET),
  paging stays off (L3), and S-mode CSRs are still not transported -- an
  S-mode ROI that reads `stvec`/`sscratch`/... sees vsim reset values.
- e2e: `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` (CHECK_PRIV=1/0) on the
  S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`.

The old one-line-per-side hardcode is gone; only the plugin's atexit
count record (no vCPU context, minstret-only consumer) keeps a static 3:

### L7. No check that the workload fits guest RAM; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.
  `--mem-size` sizes every leg up to 2G (driver mmap = QEMU memory backend
  = vsim RAM window), so the old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap"
  was misleading. The real limitation is the missing fit check plus the
  2 GiB ceiling.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption or a confusing crash; nothing tells the user `--mem-size` was
  the cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the
  driver pre-caps at the same value -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Also unchecked: the V scratch region (4 KiB at GPA `0x00FF0000`) sits
  inside RAM and nothing verifies the ELF avoids it; a segment overlapping
  it is clobbered by the V sweep on hybrid V runs.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:175` (128 MB default) and `:183` (2G pre-cap);
  `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:73` (DRAM window) and `:1362` (ram_size
  check); `verilator/src/main.cpp:414` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`). The driver already parses ELF headers for PC
  resolution (`driver/elf_syms.hpp`), so a PT_LOAD-vs-mem-size startup
  check would be cheap to add.
- Status: OPEN (the fit check). Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough
  by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5); > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN.

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`), and the V-register scratch address is the
  constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), only
  correct when RAM base is 0 (true for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt`
  where it would need 0x80FF0000). The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED (2026-06): engine variant + VLEN are pluggable;
  the machine, the CPU family, and the scratch GPA still block porting to
  another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to

  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,

  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc only, dev tier) re-runs the ELF
  on a pure-QEMU oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field
  (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:245-282`); `--cosim [--cosim-interval N]` goes
  further and localizes a divergence to the first bad N-retire window
  (it suppresses the cycle figure - the checkpoint drains pollute it; rerun
  without `--cosim` to measure). Both are manual, not CI-wired. The icount
  trigger and the SimPoint pipeline (`hsim.py`) still assert only exit code
  and PC range - a wrong register value there passes silently.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:156` (marker/pc gate), `:245-282` (oracle);
  `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`) - unchecked.
- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by
  `--verify`/`--cosim`; icount + simpoint coverage and CI wiring still OPEN.

### L22. Lock-step co-sim cannot handle asynchronous interrupts  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bites: a `--model cycle --cosim` DV run whose testbench takes a
  timer / software / external interrupt (anything NOT caused by the current
  instruction). Synchronous exceptions (`ecall`, illegal, `mret`) ARE
  supported - this is only about async interrupts.
- What happens: the QEMU oracle and the RTL DUT run on independent clocks
  (QEMU is functional with no real cycles, the RTL is cycle-accurate), so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.
  Records are aligned by attempt index, so from the interrupt onward every
  record compares handler-vs-mainloop and the diff reports a flood of false
  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.
- Where: `cosim_redesign.md` Usage 1 ("Out of scope / hard assumptions");
  the lock-step path in `driver/cosim_lockstep.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.cpp`.
- Status: OPEN. Designed fix is the opt-in `--cosim-async` mode (the RTL
  leads the interrupt schedule, QEMU replays it via an inject hook + a
  frozen timer) - features F8-F10 in `cosim_redesign.md`, not yet built.
  Distinct from L4 / the ROI envelope rule, which make the HYBRID
  measurement window interrupt-free; L22 is the lock-step DV path, which
  otherwise DOES support synchronous traps.

### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 silently skipped

- The QEMU2 leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when the
  stub did not advertise one. The leg no longer exists.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub timeout + racy port pick

- The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with

- Status: REMOVED.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no
  byte-swap path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror (golden only) uses
  a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:28-31`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent
  mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:28-31`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

The QEMU2 handback leg has been removed entirely (2026-06-09). The
simulator is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains architectural state to the
`hybrid_state_v1` file and exits; vsim resumes from that file, runs the
ROI cycle-accurately, and drains again. There is no third phase.
`CLAUDE.md` and `USER_GUIDE.md` have been updated to match; only older
architecture notes that still describe a QEMU2 spawn or a gdbstub
P-packet restore are stale - that code path no longer exists.

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: five areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor, and L11 is now
> resolved (2026-06-12): the wire format carries VLEN 128..1024 and an
> over-ceiling vlenb aborts loudly instead of truncating (L10 partial); the marker

> now round-trips with an FP-rounding fixture in the e2e suite (L20
> resolved - five CSRs restore into vsim now, and the silent FP-rounding
> gap in blocker 1 below is closed). L6 is resolved (2026-06-13): the privilege
> level round-trips (plugin gdbstub `priv` -> `dcsr.prv` write+verify ->
> exit-drain readback), S/U handoffs mirror the producer's PMP block
> (L2 partial), an M-only engine aborts loudly, and `rt_priv_smode` /
> `rt_priv_umode` run in the e2e suite on the ax66_makatau engine. The
> remaining state coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L5, L21) are
> unchanged, so the overall scores below still stand.

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be single-privilege (M/S/U since L6), trap-free, paging-off (L1-L5). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | ~~No S/U mode~~ (L6 2026-06-13), ~~no fcsr~~ (L20); still no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding (rt_c_fcsr) and S/U-privilege (rt_priv_*) covered now; still no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** ~~`fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip
   (L20)~~ - resolved 2026-06-12; `fcsr` now transports and `--verify`
   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** ~~M-mode only~~ (S/U privilege
   transports since L6, 2026-06-13, on an S/U-capable engine), but "no
   traps, no paging, no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L5) still
   rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any
   driver code, anything with page faults. The vplat runtime covers
   bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 5 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle,
   minstret, fcsr), plus `dcsr.prv` and - for S/U handoffs - the PMP
   block (L6, 2026-06-13). `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`, `mscratch`,
   `mip/mie` (and PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never written
   back into vsim (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata ate 16 bytes, fcsr another
   8; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

8	//                  mepc, then trigger the entry handoff.
9	// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.  vsim does not modify these CSRs; they must
10	//                  pass through the input-state snapshot kept by
11	//                  HandoffController and arrive at QEMU 2 unchanged.

13	//                  the CSR index of the first mismatch (1=mscratch,

/* andes_sim/roi.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andes_sim_roi_begin()/andes_sim_roi_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--model hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --model fast, --model cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ROI_H
#define ANDES_SIM_ROI_H

static inline void andes_sim_roi_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andes_sim_roi_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDES_SIM_ROI_H */

This is the key finding. `rt_csr_survival.S` is a **stale fixture from the deleted 3-phase design**: its header says "M-mode CSRs survive QEMU1 -> vsim -> **QEMU2**" and its `phase_c` (the `csrr` readback + compare) sits *after* the exit marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A1`. With the QEMU2 leg removed, vsim drains and exits **at** the exit marker — so `phase_c` never runs. The repo's own guard for "mscratch/mtvec/mepc survive the handoff" is dead code.

And the code confirms the break: `resume_driver.hpp` never restores `mscratch`, and `drain_with_passthrough` never re-reads it. So a bare-metal program that uses `mscratch` across the ROI gets wrong results — no trap, no interrupt needed.

## The program: `tests/fixtures/break_mscratch.S`

Bare-metal, single privilege (M), no async interrupt, no trap, no paging, no atomics. It only uses `mscratch` (CSR 0x340) - the standard M-mode software scratch register - across the ROI:

```asm
li   a1, 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF
csrw mscratch, a1        # stash a value BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg)
slti x0, x0, 0x5A0       # ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim
csrr a0, mscratch        # read it back INSIDE the ROI
csrw mscratch, 0xBADC... # overwrite it INSIDE the ROI
slti x0, x0, 0x5A1       # EXIT -> vsim drains + exits
```

## Proof (the simulator's own `--verify` oracle flags it)

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0xcafebabedeadbeef got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (110 fields compared)
```

`a0` (x10) read `mscratch` inside the ROI: pure-QEMU = the stashed value, vsim = `0x0`. The value never crossed the handoff.

## Root cause (two halves, same CSR)

1. **Resume gap** - `resume_driver.hpp:115` restores `mstatus/mtvec/mcycle/minstret/fcsr` (+`dcsr.prv`/PMP for S/U) but never writes `mscratch`. So the in-ROI read returns vsim's reset value.
2. **Drain gap** - `state_drain.hpp:75` (`drain_with_passthrough`) re-reads GPRs/FPR/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret from vsim but passes `mscratch` through from the QEMU1 snapshot. So the in-ROI write is silently dropped from the drained state.

## Why this is not just "a known limitation"

The notebook's core rule (cell-5) says a vsim ROI is safe if it is single-privilege, trap-free, paging-off, PMP-static, no-semihosting, no-atomics, no-MMIO. **My program satisfies every one of those** and is still silently wrong. The envelope list is incomplete - it omits "do not use a drained-but-unrestored M-CSR (`mscratch`, `mepc`, ... ) across the ROI." `mscratch` is listed in the inventory (cell-6/cell-17) as "carried but not restored," but it has no L-id and is framed as a *trap* concern; a plain trap-free program using the M-mode scratch register is exactly the case the docs say is supported.

- **Drain gap** (write-side loss) is undocumented (L4 only covers the trap triple).
- **`--verify` is blind to it**: `state_diff.cpp:22` excludes passthrough CSRs ("counters and passthrough CSRs excluded"), so a program that leaves its result in `mscratch` produces a wrong drained state that `--verify` rates PASS.

With the QEMU2 leg deleted, vsim drains+exits at the exit marker, so `phase_c` never runs. This property has been unguarded since the 3-phase design was removed.
